input: Find out if my neighborhood has a community tool shed

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether they want just a tool shed specifically, or any form of tool lending (library, co-op, community center program) changes where to look and what counts as a match.
Their specific location (city, neighborhood, zip code) determines which directories, local groups, or municipal resources are actually relevant to search.
Whether this is for personal use, a specific project, or on behalf of a community group affects how urgently they need access and how formal the process needs to be.
If they have a deadline (e.g., a weekend project), that changes the priority and speed of the search versus a leisurely exploration.
Knowing their preferred research method (online search, phone calls, in-person visits, social media) shapes the action plan they can realistically follow.
Understanding what 'found it' means to them — a confirmed address, a contact name, proof of membership eligibility — defines when the task is actually complete.
Their willingness to expand the search radius (e.g., a neighboring district or town) if nothing exists locally affects whether the plan includes fallback options.

gold.taskTitle: Find a community tool shed in your neighborhood
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to discover whether their local neighborhood has a shared community tool lending program or tool shed they can access.

questions.title: Are you open to tool libraries or lending programs too?
questions.description: Clarify whether the search is strictly for a physical 'tool shed' or includes any form of community tool sharing, such as a library lending program or co-op.

questions.title: What city, neighborhood, or zip code are you in?
questions.description: Establish the specific location so that searches can be targeted to relevant local directories, municipal websites, and community groups.

questions.title: Is this for a personal project or a group effort?
questions.description: Determine who needs access to the tools to understand the scale of borrowing needed and whether individual or organizational membership is required.

questions.title: Do you need access by a specific date or deadline?
questions.description: Find out if there is a time-sensitive project driving this search, which would prioritize speed and direct outreach over a more thorough investigation.

questions.title: How do you prefer to search — online, calls, or in person?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred research channel so the action steps match what they can realistically do (e.g., Nextdoor post, Google search, visiting a community center).

questions.title: What would confirm this task is fully done for you?
questions.description: Clarify the end goal — whether they need a confirmed address, a membership sign-up, a phone number, or simply a yes/no answer about existence.

questions.title: Would you consider a tool shed in a nearby neighborhood?
questions.description: Determine if the user is willing to expand the search radius if nothing exists in their immediate neighborhood, so fallback options can be built into the plan.
